subject: Request: per-account quantization policy for Omega Health (deal OMEGA-ENT-2026)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@omegahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: per-account quantization policy for Omega Health (deal OMEGA-ENT-2026)

Kara — looping engineering and product on a customer ask so we can surface feasibility and timelines to the Omega procurement team (James is on thread).

Summary: Omega wants the ability to define per-account quantization policies for model inference. Their goals are: lower per-token cost for internal batch workloads using 4-bit quantization while preserving high-quality (95% of current accuracy) for interactive clinician prompts. They want the option to pin a specific quant profile per account and have an automated fallback to a higher-precision variant for critical routes (e.g., diagnosis summary).

Attachments: omega-metrics-quant-report.pdf (customer perf/cost baseline), mvp-workaround-design.md (internal sketch).

Asks for Eng/Product:
- Feasibility assessment: can runtime accept per-account "quant profile" metadata and choose model variant or quant path?
- Short-term workaround options (config, route-level pinning, or model variant mapping).
- Rough estimate: effort (SWE weeks), risk, and earliest pilot date.

Customer constraints (from Kara):
- 99th pct latency target for interactive routes: <= 350ms
- Batch throughput: ~1.2M tokens/day during pilot window
- Hard procurement timeline: decision by 2026-12-10 (they need an Exec-level commitment)

Next steps: please reply with a feasibility note by EOD 11/30 so I can share with Omega and include in the MAP. Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@omegahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: per-account quantization policy for Omega Health (deal OMEGA-ENT-2026)

Marissa — quick read-through and initial thoughts. High-level: technically doable but with trade-offs. Two engineering approaches I see: 

1) Variant pinning at routing layer (low risk):
   - Expose a per-account routing flag that pins to a pre-quantized model artifact (e.g., model-q4, model-q8).
   - Runtime picks the pinned artifact; if artifact unavailable, fallback to default model.
   - Work: moderate (2–3 sprints to add pinning UI/config + runtime routing change).
   - Pros: predictable latency, minimal runtime changes.
   - Cons: needs separate artifacts for each quant profile, more storage and CI work on model builds.

2) Dynamic quant selection in runtime (higher risk):
   - Runtime honors a request header/metadata and dynamically uses quant kernels or switching codepath.
   - Could reuse single artifact with multiple kernels if we support dynamic quant tables.
   - Work: higher (3–6 sprints), more testing for correctness and perf; possible kernel-level engineering.

Important clarifying questions for Omega (please confirm):
- Which routes must guarantee the 99th-pct latency? (interactive only or also batch?)
- How tolerant are they to occasional 10–15% accuracy regression on non-critical routes?
- Will they accept a phased approach (pinning pilot first, dynamic selection later)?

Short-term workaround I can implement quickly: route-level pin + automated fallback to higher-precision variant. That would meet latency targets for interactive routes and give us a controlled pilot.

I'll draft an engineering estimate if we commit to option 1.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@omegahealth.com>, James Liao <james.liao@omegahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: per-account quantization policy for Omega Health (deal OMEGA-ENT-2026)

Thanks Dev — answers inline and additional details from Omega below: 

- Critical routes: interactive clinician prompts (roughly 60% of pilot traffic) must meet the 99th-pct latency target. Batch jobs (nightly summarization) can tolerate higher latency but need cost reduction.
- Accuracy tolerance: they will accept up to a 7% drop on non-critical batch routes; critical routes must remain within 3% of current quality metrics.
- Phased approach: yes, Omega prefers a pilot with pinned quant artifacts first and then iterate to dynamic selection.

Pilot load estimates:
- Peak QPS for interactive routes during pilot: ~18 rps (p95 requests are small, avg tokens per request ~80).
- Batch: 1.2M tokens/day (as noted).

Customer wants a firm pilot start date within 6 weeks so procurement can finalize the SOW. Their deadline for a product commitment is 2026-12-10.

If product/eng can provide a prioritized ask (option 1 pilot timeline + must-haves), I will escalate to the customer and include in the MAP (attached).

—Marissa

From: Kara Simmons <kara.simmons@omegahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: per-account quantization policy for Omega Health (deal OMEGA-ENT-2026)

Marissa — thanks for routing this internally. Confirming Omega is comfortable with a phased approach: pilot must deliver pinned quant artifacts for interactive routes with fallback behavior. If the pilot meets the stated latency and accuracy SLOs, we will include the feature in the SOW. Procurement needs a written feasibility note and a pilot ETA to proceed.

We can be flexible on token pricing during pilot. If it helps, we can allow a capped pilot spend to reduce risk for Redwood while the pilot runs.

Kara
Director of AI Integrations
Omega Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: per-account quantization policy for Omega Health (deal OMEGA-ENT-2026)

Thanks — product view & proposed ask for prioritization. I recommended we pursue option 1 (variant pinning) as a targeted enterprise feature with the following scope: 

MVP (pilot-targeted, 4 weeks dev + 2 weeks pilot):
- Routing flag that allows account-level artifact pin (UI + API config).
- Runtime fallback to default artifact when pinned artifact is not available.
- Telemetry: per-account latency, accuracy sampling, and rollout controls in Console.
- Docs + onboarding playbook for customers.

Dependencies and risks:
- Need 1 full-time SWE (runtime) + 0.5 SWE (platform) for 4 weeks; QA/engops support for pilot; model team to produce pre-quantized artifacts.
- Risk: storage/binary artifact proliferation and CI overhead.

Trade-offs: this is a near-term enterprise-only feature; it will delay one lower-priority infra improvement by a sprint. Given Omega's timeline and ARR potential (see HubSpot link), I propose we elevate this to "high" priority for the next sprint planning and seek exec alignment for the trade-off.

If we get a green light today, we can commit to a pilot kickoff window starting ~2026-12-20 pending model artifacts from the model team.

Neha Kapoor
Group Product Manager, Inference Platform
